request.prompt: ONE single cinematic main title theme for an emotional South Indian family drama: a daughter comes home to her old father in a seaside village after ten years apart. The whole track is built on ONE memorable, aching melody that returns again and again; nothing unrelated is introduced, it grows only through instruments and energy, one continuous story. Raga Charukesi (a Mixolydian flat-six scale) in D: D E F# G A Bb C. The melody starts bright in the low notes D E F# G, then leans on the flat sixth Bb and falls Bb A G F# like a sob; that turn is the emotion. Rising phrases climb A Bb C D, falling phrases come down D C Bb A G F# E D. Sung-style phrasing with gamakam: slides into notes, a wide shake on F# and Bb, grace notes before long notes. Modal harmony on a D pedal with a soft drone on D and A, few chord changes, no Western chord loops. One steady pulse: a gentle 6/8 sway at 76 BPM from 22 s to the end, never stopping. The voice: a soft, close, natural wordless female humming voice (mm and aa) carries the melody. Real instruments, played by real musicians, close, dry and natural, no heavy echo or delay, not chopped: bamboo flute, violin section in Indian-style unison, solo violin, tabla, soft felt piano, warm round bass. A separate quiet electronic layer: a chopped glitching veena answering phrases, a pitched-down mridangam low hit, a reversed veena swell before the big return. 0-8 s: only a lone bamboo flute plays a rising 3-note call D F A with the last note bent up, over the soft drone, dawn by the sea. 8-22 s: the female humming sings the melody softly and alone, the chopped veena answers each phrase quietly. 22-40 s: a gentle tabla sway and warm bass start, violins softly under the humming, tender memories of childhood. 40-50 s: the drums thin to a light pulse, a solo violin plays the bitter turn on Bb, the humming holds one long aching note; still moving, no silence. 50-72 s: a reversed veena swell and one deep low hit, then the melody returns at its fullest, a whole step higher in E: humming, violins and flute in unison, full tabla groove and bass, a warm tearful reunion, hopeful. 72-90 s: the music softens, the humming sings the first phrase once more, the flute ends alone on the 3-note call, a last warm note held over the drone. No section that sounds like a different song, no silences, no gaps, no EDM, no trailer drums, not a hero or royal march, no heavy echo on the flute or voice, no lyrics.
